## Szmelc global rules
> Install: `./install.sh` links this file as the global instructions of every detected harness (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`, `~/.qwen/QWEN.md`, `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`, …). Conventions repo: `~/.config/szmelc/conventions` (missing → `git clone https://github.com/Szmelc-INC/CONVENTIONS.md ~/.config/szmelc/conventions && ~/.config/szmelc/conventions/install.sh`). Paths below are relative to that repo.

### Always
- Chat: Polish. Code, comments, docs, commits: English.
- Never `sudo`; use `pkexec`.
- Autonomous end to end (push, CI, fix, retry). Ask only before destructive/irreversible: deletion, force-push, history rewrite, visibility/permission change, prod data.
- Bad request → say why in one line, then do the best version.
- Never change another repo without asking; when a dependency fails, name the repo and the cause.
- Subagents: never spawn unless the user explicitly asks; see `AGENTS/RULES/SUBAGENTS.md`.
- Precedence: user's direct instruction > project `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` > these rules.

### Lazy conventions (token rule)
- Read `INDEX.md` once per session. Load only files whose trigger matches the current task. Never bulk-read the repo; never re-read a loaded file.
- No match → no extra reads.
- Stable rules only. `CONVENTIONS/EXPERIMENTAL/` only when the user opts in; `CONVENTIONS/LEGACY/` only when asked.
- Never load `CONVENTIONS.md` (the all-in-one bundle) together with `INDEX.md`; it is for tools that cannot lazy-load.

### Triage every task
- **Trivial** (typo, rename, config tweak, obvious one-file fix, factual Q): act now, no plan, reply 1–3 lines.
- **Normal** (feature in known code, clear bug): read what the change touches, implement, verify once, short report.
- **Hard** (architecture, cross-cutting refactor, unclear root cause, security, new project): use skill `deep` (`AGENTS/skills/deep/SKILL.md`) before coding.

### Spend vs save
- Save: search (grep/glob) then read ranges, not whole files; batch independent calls; no narration, recaps or restating; summarize big outputs as file:line; stop exploring once you can act; quick experiment beats theorizing.
- Spend: design, root cause, security, non-trivial edge cases, creative work (be bold, offer the better idea, flag deviation in one line).
- Model, effort, context hygiene: `AGENTS/RULES/EFFICIENCY.md`.

## Token efficiency
> Load when: choosing a model or effort level, configuring a harness or subagent, writing instruction files, or a session grows long.

- Free savings, always: locate before reading; read ranges; check size (`wc -l`) before ingesting; never re-read a file after editing it; batch independent calls; stop once you can act.
- Big output (logs, test runs, JSON) → into a file, then grep/jq the part you need.
- Risky savings, weigh each time: skipping verification, cutting exploration short, a weaker model for reasoning. Never cut the quality of thinking.
- Match model and effort to difficulty: mechanical work (search, rename, move, format) → small model or low effort; design, root cause, security → strong model, high effort.
- Default effort medium; raise per task, never permanently. Pick model and effort at session start; switching mid-task can invalidate the prompt cache.
- Custom subagents pin `model` and `effort` so they never inherit the top model by accident. When to spawn at all: `AGENTS/RULES/SUBAGENTS.md`.
- Instruction files stay static, short (< ~200 lines) and index-like; an import loads at session start, so it saves nothing.
- Load tool and MCP schemas on demand; never attach servers mid-session.
- One task per session; clear between unrelated tasks; compact keeping goal, decisions, files changed, failing checks.
- No scheduled loops on idle sessions: each run resends the whole context.

## Subagents & tools
> Load when: considering a subagent, parallel work, skills/MCP use, or long-running commands.

- Never spawn a subagent unless the user explicitly asks. Search and read files directly.
- Parallel work looks worth it → ask first: how many agents and why.
- Once allowed: only for wide multi-dir/multi-repo search where only the conclusion matters, or 2+ independent streams each needing heavy reading.
- Never for: one file, known location, quick grep, < ~5 tool calls.
- Max 3 parallel. Prompt = self-contained: paths, known facts, exact deliverable. `effort: medium` unless the subtask is hard.
- Skills/MCP/plugins: only when they directly fit; never speculative loading.
- Long commands: background, keep working, check when needed.

## Shell environment & dotfiles
> Load when: building or changing a shell setup: rc files, dotfiles, plugins, prompt, shell integrations.

- The rc file is a loader only: it bootstraps and sources; real config lives in one directory (e.g. `~/.zsh/`) under git.
- Runcommands are `NN-name.zsh`, sourced in lexical order; the number encodes load order; leave gaps (00, 10, 20…).
- One concern per file; line 1 is `# NN-name.zsh — <concern>`.
- Every file is re-sourceable; guard anything order-sensitive.
- Functions: one per file, file name == function name (autoload); completions `_name`; scripts in `bin/` executable with a shebang.
- Plugins are declared in the plugin manager, never hand-cloned.
- One idempotent bootstrap brings a bare shell to the full setup; a manual step is a bug.
- Machine-local overrides and secrets in a gitignored `local/` directory, sourced last.
- Installers snapshot before changing a live setup; a user layer is never touched by upgrades.
- Baseline output: syntax highlighting, colored aligned listings, pickers with a live preview.
- Reference implementations: Silver-ZSH (`SHELL-INTEGRATION-BIBLE.md`), Modern-Shell.

## Go
> Load when: writing, building or releasing Go code.

- Current stable Go; `CGO_ENABLED=0`, one static binary.
- Cross-compile for linux, darwin, windows and freebsd unless the tool is Linux-only by nature.
- SQLite via `modernc.org/sqlite` (no cgo); WAL mode.
- Static web assets ship inside the binary with `embed`.
- Layout: one `main` package or `cmd/<bin>`, private code in `internal/`, tests next to the code.
- `gofmt` and `go vet` clean; every error handled or returned with context.
- Stdlib first; the Charm stack (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/TUI.md`) is the default exception.

## Naming
> Load when: naming a repo, binary, package, env var, config key, file or doc.

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Repo | `Title-Case-With-Hyphens` | `Modern-Shell`, `Linux-From-Something` |
| Binary / command | lowercase, short, one word | `msh`, `saur`, `lfn` |
| Command alias | same binary, dispatched on `argv[0]` | `px` → `silkrouter` |
| Env var | `UPPER_SNAKE` with the tool prefix | `SAUR_COLOR` |
| Config key | `snake_case`, English, never translated | `build_timeout` |
| Shell function / exported var | `snake_case` / `UPPER_SNAKE` | `build_pkg`, `SAUR_OUT` |
| Experimental package | `<name>-ex` | `saur-ex` |
| Major-version contract | `ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` | `ARCHITECTURE-v4.md` |
| Branch | `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md` | `feat/signing` |

- Names say what a user gets, not how it is built.
- No version numbers in repo or binary names; versions live in tags (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).

## Shell scripts
> Load when: writing or editing a shell script (bash, zsh, POSIX sh) or an installer.

- Shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bash` (`sh`, `zsh` when that is the target); bash scripts start with `set -euo pipefail`.
- POSIX `sh` where it costs nothing; otherwise say which shell is required.
- Tunables in a commented block at the top; the logic below never hardcodes them.
- Output through helpers with the CLI vocabulary (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CLI.md`); colors via `tput`, off when not a TTY or `NO_COLOR` is set.
- Missing tool → fallback chain (`ss` → `netstat` → `lsof`), then a clear error naming what to install.
- Idempotent: re-running converges, never duplicates or breaks state.
- Quote every expansion; `$HOME` and XDG vars, never `/home/<user>`; temp files via `mktemp`, removed on exit (`trap`).
- `bash -n` / `sh -n` and `shellcheck` clean before delivery.
- Root: never `sudo`; `pkexec` for the one step that needs it.

## Stack defaults
> Load when: starting a project or tool, or choosing a language or dependencies.

- Minimal deps: write or cherry-pick the snippet before pulling a library for one small task.
- CLI / TUI / daemons: Go, stdlib-first (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/GO.md`, `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CLI.md`, `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/TUI.md`).
- Glue and installers: shell (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/SHELL.md`). Never add a runtime (node, python) for what shell or Go does in a few lines.
- Web UI: static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step to run; frameworks only when the UI really needs them.
- Python only where its ecosystem is the point (ML, data); keep the core light and heavy stacks optional.
- Config-driven and modular where it costs little: behavior in config and plugins, not hardcoded (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`).
- Platforms: Arch first (reference, CI-tested), then Nix and other Linux, Windows via WSL2, macOS best effort; no hardcoded `/home/...` paths.

## Colors
> Load when: any UI, TUI, CLI color, web page, theme, badge or graphic.

| Role | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Accent | `#105c5c` | On dark: fill + white text |
| Accent text/links | `#1f8a8a` | Text, links |
| Danger/experimental | `#750f0f` / `#b83a3a` text | Errors, warnings, experimental |
| Silver | `#c0c0c0` | Secondary |
| Aquamarine | `#7fffd4` | Max 1–2 highlights per screen, black text |
| Neutrals | `#0b0b0b` `#131313` `#1b1b1b`, lines `#262626` | Everything else |
| Light neutrals | `#f3f3f3` `#ffffff` `#e9e9e9`, lines `#d6d6d6`, text `#141414` | Light toggle only |

- Dark by default; light only as a toggle. Never purple, never a framework's default accent.
- Neutrals carry no blue or green tint.
- Badges, banners and shields use the same palette: `105c5c` fill, `c0c0c0` for secondary values, `750f0f` for experimental.
- Project has config → make colors configurable.

## CI
> Load when: setting up or changing CI checks or required status checks, or fixing a red CI run.

- `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs on every push and PR, without a `paths:` filter.
- It runs format + lint, build, tests, package build, docs-in-sync; cheap steps first, fail fast, no `continue-on-error` on required steps.
- Lint per stack: `shellcheck` for shell, `go vet` + `gofmt -l` for Go, the ecosystem's standard linter elsewhere.
- Package build: `PKGBUILD` in an Arch container, `nix build` when a flake ships (`CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`, `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md`).
- Docs-in-sync: regenerate generated files, `--help` output and completions, then `git diff --exit-code`.
- Tests run on throwaway state (temp `HOME`, temp dirs), never on real user config.
- Required checks (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`) match job names: keep them stable; renaming a job blocks merges until the ruleset is updated.
- On failure, upload logs and test output: `actions/upload-artifact` with `if: failure()` and a short `retention-days`.
- CI never pushes to `main`. Exception: bots listed in one place (README "Automation" section), pushing via a ruleset bypass actor or a PR.
- Schedule heartbeat bot: commits one file (`.github/heartbeat`) only after ~45 quiet days, never daily.
- Red CI: read `gh run view <id> --log-failed`, reproduce with the local script, fix, push; never rerun until green.

## Workflows
> Load when: writing or editing a GitHub Actions workflow, reusable workflow or composite action.

- One purpose per file in `.github/workflows/`: `check.yml` (CI), `release.yml` (releases), `pages.yml` (site).
- Triggers: `push` + `pull_request` for checks; add `workflow_dispatch` to anything worth rerunning by hand.
- `schedule` only for data from outside the repo; public repos disable it after 60 days without activity, so add a heartbeat (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`).
- Cross-repo triggers: `repository_dispatch` with a named `types:` entry.
- Top-level `permissions: contents: read`; elevate per job only (`contents: write`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`).
- `concurrency:` group per workflow + ref; `cancel-in-progress: true` for checks, `false` for deploys and releases.
- Pin actions to a major tag (`actions/*`) or a full commit SHA with a `# vX` comment (third-party); Dependabot keeps them current (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md`).
- Logic lives in repo scripts that run locally (Docker/Podman when the host differs); the workflow only checks out, sets up and calls them.
- Pass `${{ }}` values into `run:` through `env:`, never inline (script injection).
- Secrets only via `secrets.*` or OIDC (`id-token: write`); never echo them or put them on a command line; mask derived values with `::add-mask::`.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` over PATs. Events it causes start no workflows (except `workflow_dispatch`/`repository_dispatch`) and it cannot reach other repos; for those cases only, use a GitHub App token (`actions/create-github-app-token`) or a fine-grained PAT scoped to the target repo.
- Same steps in 2+ repos → reusable workflow (`on: workflow_call`) or composite action in one org repo, called pinned.
- Results people read go to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` as Markdown, not only to logs.
- Minutes: public repos run free on standard runners, private repos on GitHub Free get 2,000 min/month; keep matrices to supported targets, cache dependencies (`actions/cache` or a setup action's `cache:`).

## Code security
> Load when: creating a repo, adding dependencies, or handling Dependabot, secret-scanning or code-scanning alerts.

- Dependabot alerts and security updates on for every repo.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: version updates for `github-actions` plus each package ecosystem, `interval: weekly`, `groups:` to batch minor/patch.
- Dependabot PRs follow the normal PR flow; merge when CI is green, never skip checks.
- Secret scanning + push protection on (`gh repo edit --enable-secret-scanning --enable-secret-scanning-push-protection`; free for public repos).
- Leaked secret: rotate it first, then remove it; history rewriting needs owner approval.
- CodeQL default setup for supported languages (free for public repos); fix or dismiss alerts with a reason.
- Private vulnerability reporting on for public repos; policy file: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SECURITY-MD.md`.
- Never commit secrets, tokens or `.env` files; workflows read them per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`.

## Coding agents on GitHub
> Load when: assigning issues to a coding agent, @-mentioning an agent on GitHub, or running an agent from a workflow.

- Agents: Copilot coding agent (assign an issue; needs a paid Copilot plan), Claude Code / Codex GitHub apps or actions (@-mention or workflow).
- Agent PRs follow the same rules: titles per `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md`, flow per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PULL-REQUESTS.md`.
- Branch names per `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md` where the tool allows (e.g. a branch-prefix input); fixed tool prefixes are accepted.
- Agent PRs stay draft until checks are green; a human or the orchestrating agent reviews and merges, never the agent itself unasked.
- Instructions come from the repo `AGENTS.md`; `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` are generated from it (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/AGENTS-MD.md`).
- Issue for an agent: one task, acceptance criteria, files or commands to run; same as for a human.
- Least-privilege tokens: repo-scoped, contents + pull requests + issues only; workflow `permissions:` set explicitly.
- Never put secrets in prompts, issues or comments; agents read them from Actions secrets only.
- Untrusted input (issues or comments from strangers) never triggers an agent with write access.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/ENVIRONMENTS.md -->
## Deployment environments
> Load when: deploying anything from Actions, or adding deployment secrets.

- Every deploy job declares `environment:` with `name` (`github-pages`, `production`) and `url` from the deploy step's output.
- Deployment branches: `main` only (tags `v*` for release deploys).
- Secrets used only by one deploy are environment secrets, not repo secrets.
- Required reviewers or wait timers only when a second human can approve; solo repos rely on the branch policy.
- GitHub Free: environment secrets and branch policies work in public repos only; private repos use repo secrets and deploy only from `main`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/GITHUB-PAGES.md -->
## GitHub Pages
> Load when: publishing a site, docs or web UI on GitHub Pages.

- Source "GitHub Actions" (`gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -f build_type=workflow`); never a `gh-pages` branch.
- Build job → `actions/upload-pages-artifact`; deploy job → `actions/deploy-pages` with `pages: write`, `id-token: write`, environment `github-pages` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/ENVIRONMENTS.md`).
- Never commit build output; the output dir (`public/`) is gitignored.
- Build script lives in the repo and gives the same result locally; the workflow only calls it.
- Output: one self-contained `index.html` (CSS, JS, data inlined) that works offline and over `file://`.
- Next to it: the same data as JSON; docs sites also ship `llms.txt` (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LLMS-TXT.md`).
- Deploy only from `main`; triggers: push on source paths, `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch` for refreshes from other repos.
- Nightly `schedule` only when data comes from outside the repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`).
- Repo homepage = the Pages URL unless a real site exists (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`).
- Custom domain only when one is owned: set it in Pages settings (`gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pages -f cname=<domain>`); Actions deploys ignore a `CNAME` file.
- Look and feel: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/WEBUI-STYLE.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/WEBUI-STYLE.md -->
## Web UI style
> Load when: building or restyling a Szmelc web page, Pages site or web UI.

- Reference look: <https://szmelc-inc.github.io/SAUR/>.
- Colors only from `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`, as CSS custom properties on `:root`.
- Dark by default; light via a toggle (`data-theme` on `<html>`), choice kept in `localStorage` inside `try`/`catch`.
- Monospace everywhere: `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`; never fetch webfonts.
- Flat mono/material look: 1px lines `#262626`, radius 0–4px; no gradients, glassmorphism or heavy shadows.
- Header: small `h1` (≤ 1.5rem, no hero), accent top rule (`border-top` 3–4px accent), stats row of counts below.
- Navigation: folder-style tabs; keys `/` focus filter, `1`–`9` switch tabs, `esc` clear/close; deep links `#<path>` restore the view on load.
- Install: one copyable command block with a copy button.
- Icons: inline SVG with `currentColor`; no icon fonts or icon CDNs.
- Effects stay subtle (hover underline or glow, blinking cursor); none under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- Contrast WCAG AA in both themes; visible keyboard focus.
- No tracking, analytics or cookies; external JS only when unavoidable, from a CDN URL pinned to an exact version with `integrity`.
- Works at 360px width: no horizontal page scroll; wide tables and code scroll inside their own box.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DISCUSSIONS.md -->
## Discussions
> Load when: enabling GitHub Discussions, choosing categories, or moving threads between issues and discussions.

- Enable only when the project has users beyond its maintainers (`gh repo edit --enable-discussions`); otherwise issues suffice.
- Categories: Announcements (maintainers post), Ideas, Q&A (answerable), Show and tell; delete unused defaults.
- Issues are actionable work; questions, ideas and open-ended talk are discussions.
- Convert a non-actionable issue to a discussion; open an issue from a discussion once work is agreed, linking both ways.
- Accepted idea → proposal PR on an experimental branch (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md`); link the discussion in the PR.
- Q&A: mark the answer; turn repeated questions into docs.
- Release and breaking-change notes go to Announcements.
- CLI: `gh discussion list/view/create/comment` (preview); otherwise `gh api graphql`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ISSUES.md -->
## Issues
> Load when: creating, triaging or closing issues, or adding issue templates.

- Issue forms: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/<name>.yml` (bug, feature) with `labels:` preset; org default in the org `.github` repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`: `blank_issues_enabled: false`; `contact_links` to Discussions, docs or support.
- Title: imperative, specific, no type prefix (`Fix crash on empty config`, `Add --json to list`); type goes in the label.
- Label on creation (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`); set the issue type when the org defines types (`--type Bug`).
- Split work into sub-issues (`gh issue create --parent <n>`, `gh issue edit <n> --add-sub-issue <m>`); short checklists stay `- [ ]` task lists.
- Dependencies: `--blocked-by <n>` / `--blocking <n>`, not prose.
- Close via the PR: `Closes #<n>` in the PR body; keywords only fire when the PR targets the default branch.
- Closing without a PR: comment why, close as not planned or duplicate (`gh issue close <n> -r "not planned" -c "<why>"`).
- Roadmap: one issue with sub-issues, pinned (`gh issue pin <n>`); max 3 pinned.
- Agents: `gh issue list/view/create/edit/comment` with `--json`; never close an issue you did not resolve.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md -->
## Organizations
> Load when: creating or maintaining a GitHub organization, its profile, teams, or org-wide defaults.

- Org profile: public `.github` repo with `profile/README.md` (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`).
- Org `.github` repo holds default community health files, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; repos override only when they differ.
- Access through teams with least privilege, never per-person grants on each repo.
- Pin up to 6 flagship repos on the org profile.
- Every repo: consistent name (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/NAMING.md`), description, homepage, topics (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`).
- Same labels and settings everywhere (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`, `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`).
- Cross-repo planning: org-level Projects (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PROJECTS.md`).
- Org settings, membership and repo visibility: owner approval first.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PROJECTS.md -->
## Projects
> Load when: planning work across issues, creating or editing a GitHub Project board.

- Projects (v2) only; one per org or per initiative, not one per repo.
- Items are issues and PRs; draft items only for quick capture, converted to issues before work starts.
- Fields: Status (Todo, In progress, Done), Priority (P0–P2), Size (S/M/L), Iteration when working in cycles.
- Views: Board grouped by Status, Table for triage, Roadmap by Iteration or dates.
- Built-in workflows: auto-add matching repo issues/PRs, item added → Todo, item closed and PR merged → Done.
- Status follows issues and PRs (open, linked PR, closed), not hand-moved cards.
- Link the project to its repos (`gh project link`).
- CLI: `gh project view/item-list/item-add/item-edit/field-list --owner <org>`; needs the `project` scope (`gh auth refresh -s project`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PULL-REQUESTS.md -->
## Pull requests
> Load when: committing, pushing, or opening/reviewing/merging a PR.

- Self-review before PR: correctness, security/escaping, docs + shell completions in sync.
- Work in progress → draft PR (`gh pr create --draft`); `gh pr ready` only when done and self-reviewed.
- Body follows `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (what, why, checks run); org default: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`.
- Link issues with `Closes #<n>` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ISSUES.md`); label on creation (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`).
- Review: concrete fixes as suggested changes (a `suggestion` code block); the author batch-applies them as one commit.
- Wait for green CI → merge yourself → verify main CI + live result → one short report.
- Checks still running → `gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch`; verify after it lands all the same.
- Never merge red, force-push, or bypass branch protection; repo settings: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`.
- What CI runs and requires: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`; workflow files: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`.
- Commit and PR titles: `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/AUTOMATION.md -->
## Release automation
> Load when: writing or running a release workflow or script, attaching release assets, or bumping downstream packages.

- Default: a human pushes the tag (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md`); `.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest.
- Trigger `on: push: tags: ['v*']`, plus `workflow_dispatch` with a tag input for reruns.
- A tag pushed by a workflow with `GITHUB_TOKEN` triggers nothing; dispatch the release instead (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/WORKFLOWS.md`).
- `contents: write` on the release job only.
- Build every asset on CI from the tag; never upload local builds.
- Attach assets + `SHA256SUMS` (`sha256sum <assets> > SHA256SUMS`), plus a signature (`SHA256SUMS.sig`) when the project signs.
- Publish: `gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --notes-from-tag <assets>`; no curated notes → `--generate-notes`; `-rc.N` → add `--prerelease`.
- `.github/release.yml` groups generated notes by label (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md`): `changelog.categories` for `feat`, `bug`, `docs`, `chore`, last one `"*"`.
- Release logic is a repo script that runs locally with `--dry-run`: builds, checksums, prints the `gh` commands without publishing.
- Downstream bumps after publish: `PKGBUILD`/SAUR and `flake.nix` via PR, or `repository_dispatch` to the packaging repo.
- Verify: `gh release view "$TAG"` lists every asset, checksums match, downstream PRs green.
- Release-please style automation only when the project uses Conventional Commits strictly (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md -->
## Release channels
> Load when: deciding where a build is published: stable, pre-release, experimental or nightly.

| Channel | Built from | Tag | GitHub release |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stable | `main` | `vX.Y.Z` | Normal, marked Latest |
| Pre-release | `main` | `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | `--prerelease` |
| Experimental | any other branch | none | none |
| Nightly (optional) | `main`, scheduled | `nightly`, rolling | `--prerelease --latest=false` |

- Latest = newest stable; never mark a pre-release or nightly as latest.
- Experimental: `-ex` in package name or version, installs next to stable; ships as workflow artifacts or a package channel (Arch: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`).
- Nightly is the only tag and release that is re-created: `gh release delete nightly --cleanup-tag -y`, then `gh release create nightly --target main --prerelease --latest=false`.
- Nightly only when people test unreleased builds; skip the run when `main` has not changed.
- Install docs point at stable; other channels are opt-in.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md -->
## Tags
> Load when: creating, pushing, protecting or fixing a release tag.

- Annotated only: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -F <notes-file>`; never lightweight.
- Format `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`); pre-releases `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`.
- Tag `main` only, on a commit whose CI is green.
- `-ex` builds are never tagged `v*` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`).
- Tag message: title `vX.Y.Z`, then that version's changelog section.
- Push one tag explicitly: `git push origin vX.Y.Z`; never `git push --tags`.
- Published tags are immutable: never move, delete or re-push one; fix a bad release with a new patch tag.
- Only exception: the rolling `nightly` tag (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`).
- Protect with a tag ruleset (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets`): `target: tag`, `conditions.ref_name.include: ["refs/tags/v*"]`, rules `update` + `deletion`; `nightly` stays outside it.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md -->
## Releases & versioning
> Load when: bumping a version, preparing a release, or planning a major version.

- SemVer `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Tags: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md`; publishing: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/AUTOMATION.md`; channels: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`.
- The version lives in package metadata and tags; never in the README title or repo name.
- One bump moves every copy at once: source constant, PKGBUILD `pkgver`, `flake.nix` `version`, changelog if the project keeps one.
- Breaking change to a command, flag, config key or file format → major bump, plus a new `docs/ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` when the project keeps one.
- Ecosystem eras (`SZMELC/README.md`) are independent of project versions.
- Before tagging: versions agree; `--help`, completions and README match the code; tests pass on throwaway state; the package builds in CI; the architecture contract is current.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/LABELS.md -->
## Labels
> Load when: creating, editing or applying issue/PR labels, or setting up a new repo.

- Keep the set small; plain names, no `type:` prefixes, so `--force` recolors GitHub defaults instead of duplicating them.

| Label | Color | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `bug` `feat` `docs` `chore` | `105c5c` | Type, one per issue/PR |
| `area/<x>` | `1b1b1b` | Per-project subsystem, defined in the project |
| `experimental` | `750f0f` | Proposal on an experimental branch |
| `legacy` | `c0c0c0` | Superseded material |
| `blocked` | `b83a3a` | Waiting on something external |
| `good first issue` | `7fffd4` | Easy entry; the one highlight color |
| `help wanted` | `1f8a8a` | Maintainer wants outside help |

- Colors come from `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`, hex without `#`; recolor GitHub's purple defaults.
- Labels as code: a script or `labels.tsv` in the repo, applied with `gh label create <name> -c <hex> -d <desc> --force`.
- Same set across an org: `gh label clone <source-repo> --force`.
- Never delete or rename a label others use; mark it deprecated in its description first.
- Label on creation (`gh issue create -l`, `gh pr create -l`), not afterwards.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md -->
## Repo metadata
> Load when: creating a repo, first push, release, or editing README/manifest/license.

- `gh repo view` first; fill gaps via `gh repo edit`: description, homepage, topics, badges.
- Homepage priority: real site → GitHub Pages → repo URL. Never invent.
- Keep manifest fields (package.json, go.mod, PKGBUILD, flake.nix…) in sync with repo metadata.
- License: MIT.
- Fork of someone else's project: say "independent, not affiliated" in the README and the description; add a trademark note when the upstream name is a mark.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md -->
## Repo settings
> Load when: creating a repo, changing its GitHub settings, merge options, rulesets or feature toggles.

- Apply settings as code: `gh repo edit` flags and `gh api` calls in a script, not web-UI clicks. Metadata: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`.
- Default branch `main` (`--default-branch main`); branch model: `CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md`.
- Merge: squash only (`--enable-squash-merge --enable-merge-commit=false --enable-rebase-merge=false`).
- Squash message `--squash-merge-commit-message pr-title-commits`: PR title becomes the subject, commit trailers (`Co-Authored-By:`) survive.
- `--delete-branch-on-merge`, `--enable-auto-merge`, `--allow-update-branch`.
- Ruleset on the default branch via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets` (`gh ruleset` only lists, views, checks):
  - `pull_request` with 0 required approvals: PR required, solo maintainers self-merge.
  - `required_status_checks`: only checks that run on every PR; a path-filtered or not-yet-existing check blocks merges forever.
  - `non_fast_forward`, `deletion`, `required_linear_history`.
- Rulesets are free on public repos; private repos on GitHub Free get none, so the PR flow is self-enforced there.
- Features: issues on; discussions only for a community (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DISCUSSIONS.md`); projects per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PROJECTS.md`; wiki off (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/WIKI.md`).
- Security toggles: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md`.
- Visibility change, transfer, archive or rename: owner approval first; never pass `--accept-visibility-change-consequences` on your own.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/WIKI.md -->
## Wiki
> Load when: enabling a GitHub wiki or deciding where project docs live.

- Docs live in the repo (versioned, reviewed via PR) and on Pages; the repo is the source of truth.
- Wiki off by default (`gh repo edit --enable-wiki=false`).
- Wiki only if users expect one: generate or sync it from repo docs in CI; never edit it by hand.
- The wiki never holds rules, specs or anything not also in the repo.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CLI.md -->
## CLI
> Load when: building or changing a command-line tool.

- One binary, one entry point, rich subcommands + flags + config file (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md`).
- Colored per-command help; aligned tables. Colors: `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`.
- Message prefixes: `::` info, `==>` step, `✓` ok, `!!` warn, `✗` error. Messages to stderr, data to stdout.
- `--no-color` and `NO_COLOR`; plain output when stdout is not a TTY.
- `--json` for data output.
- Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` error, `2` usage error.
- `completion <shell>` + installed zsh/bash/fish completion files, generated from the command registry.
- Destructive commands confirm (or take `--yes`) and support `--dry-run`.
- Root: `pkexec` for the one step that needs it; never `sudo`.
- Has a CLI → also needs a TUI: `CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/TUI.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CONFIG.md -->
## Configuration
> Load when: adding a config file, options, env vars, or storage paths to a tool.

- Human-edited: TOML, every option commented with its default. Machine-written: strict JSON (reject unknown keys).
- Avoid YAML for authored config (whitespace and type footguns); use it only where a tool demands it.
- Precedence, later wins: built-in defaults < config file < `*.local.*` override (gitignored) < env `TOOL_*` < flags.
- XDG paths: config `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/<tool>/`, data `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/<tool>/`, cache and state likewise. Shipped defaults stay separate from the user layer.
- Runs with zero config; an option exists only where two real users need different behavior.
- Validate on load; invalid → a clear error naming file and key, nothing applied. Never guess or coerce.
- Secrets never in config: reference an env var, file path or keyring entry by name.
- Local persistence: SQLite (WAL) when there is real data, else a plain file.
- Colors configurable when the project has config (`CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/TUI.md -->
## TUI
> Load when: building a TUI, or any project that has a CLI.

- Go: bubbletea + lipgloss + bubbles + glamour.
- Thin front-end over the same commands and functions as the CLI; no logic lives only in the TUI.
- Fully keyboard-driven; mouse is a bonus.
- `:` command palette, help overlay (`?` / F1), keybinds shown in a footer.
- Tabs per item type; add / edit / toggle / remove in place, destructive actions confirmed.
- Markdown rendered with glamour.
- Colors: `CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md -->
## Arch packaging
> Load when: packaging, releasing, or adding install instructions.

- Ship a `PKGBUILD` (repo root or a packaging subdirectory) that installs: binary, shell completions, license, docs.
- SAUR builds every PKGBUILD in the org: the default branch publishes to `[saur]`; any other branch to `[saur-ex]` as `<name>-ex`, installable next to stable.
- Override per PKGBUILD: `_saur_channel=stable|experimental|skip`.
- VCS packages: `pkgver()` yielding `r<count>.<hash>`.
- Packages, databases and install scripts are signed; clients use `SigLevel = Required`.
- Version moves with the release (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- Nix counterpart: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md`. Installers: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/INSTALL.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/INSTALL.md -->
## Install & uninstall
> Load when: writing an installer, a setup script, install instructions, or uninstall steps.

- Package first (SAUR, Nix); a script installer only for what a package cannot do (user config, harness links).
- Reversible: ship and document uninstall; it restores what install changed.
- Own one prefix (`~/.local/share/<tool>`, or one folder in portable mode); outside it, touch at most one documented hook line.
- Never overwrite user files: move them to `*.bak.<timestamp>` and restore them on uninstall.
- Idempotent: re-running converges and never duplicates.
- `status` and `--dry-run` show what would change before anything does.
- Verifiable sources: a tag or a signed script, never a branch tip piped into a shell.
- Root: `pkexec` for the one step that needs it, never for the whole script.
- Scripts follow `CONVENTIONS/CODE/SHELL.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md -->
## Nix packaging
> Load when: packaging, releasing, or setting up a dev environment.

- Ship `flake.nix` with: package, app, devShell.
- `version` in the flake moves with the release (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- Arch counterpart: `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/REPO/LAYOUT.md -->
## Repository layout
> Load when: creating a repo, adding top-level files or directories, or auditing a repo against the conventions.

| File | When | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | always | What it is, one-line install, usage, how it works (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md`) |
| `LICENSE` | always | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LICENSE.md` |
| `AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` (`@AGENTS.md`) | always | Working rules for coding agents (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/AGENTS-MD.md`) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | when kept | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CHANGELOG-MD.md` |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` | override of the org default | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CONTRIBUTING-MD.md`, `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SECURITY-MD.md`, `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CODE-OF-CONDUCT-MD.md` |
| `.github/CODEOWNERS` | ≥ 2 maintainers | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CODEOWNERS.md` |
| `.mcp.json` | shared MCP servers | `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/MCP-JSON.md` |
| `DESIGN.md` | new projects | The owner's brief (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/DESIGN-MD.md`) |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` | DB, daemon or plugin system | Binding contract per major version |
| `PKGBUILD`, `flake.nix` | anything installable | `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`, `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md` |
| CI workflow | always | Build the package and run tests on every PR (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ACTIONS/CI.md`) |

- Directories by job: source (`cmd/`, `internal/`, `src/`), `scripts/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `completions/`; packaging at the root or in a packaging subdirectory.
- One entry point: one command with subcommands, not a pile of loose scripts.
- Features are files: modules, plugins, drivers and addons live in their own directory and can be added, toggled and removed without touching the core.
- Never commit: secrets, machine-local overrides (`*.local.*`), build output, large data or model artefacts. Gitignore them.
- Superseded code moves to a legacy directory or into git history; never leave dead copies next to live ones.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/REPO/WRITING.md -->
## Writing & voice
> Load when: writing docs, help text, error messages, commit messages, or community and lore text.

- English for everything structural: code, identifiers, comments, docs, config keys, commits, logs.
- Polish for the cultural side: `README-PL.md`, community posts, lore. One language per file.
- Never translate machine-parsed identifiers (commands, config keys, schema fields, event names).
- Docs voice: plain, honest, specific. Name limits and risks. No filler adjectives ("modern", "clean", "powerful", "seamless").
- Humor (™, memes, lore) lives in profiles, banners and lore docs; never in specs, error messages or identifiers.
- `™` and other marks never appear in identifiers, package names or config.
- Dense: cut every word that does not change the meaning. Rules are imperative one-liners.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/CORE-MAPS.md -->
## Core maps
> Load when: organising a doc tree into cores, adding a core or category, or editing a core README.

- Core = UPPERCASE directory `X/` + guide `X/README.md` + generated root map `X.md`.
- `X/README.md`: line 1 `# Title`, line 2 `> Load when: <trigger>`, then what the core holds and a table of its categories.
- Root map `X.md`: generated: title, trigger, link to the guide, then `| Path | What | Load when |` rows from each file's header. Never hand-edit.
- A hand-written root file keeps its map between `<!-- map:begin -->` and `<!-- map:end -->`; only that block is generated.
- Nested categories repeat the pattern; `X/<SUB>/README.md` is optional, only when a category needs more than its table row.
- Every category directory has a row in its core guide's table.
- Any project may adopt it for a doc tree; the build script generates maps and indexes (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/INDEX-MD.md`).
- This repo: cores `CONVENTIONS/`, `AGENTS/`, `HUMANS/`, `CONTRIBUTING/`, `SZMELC/`, `META/`; root maps `CONVENTIONS.md` (bundle, opens with the map), `AGENTS.md` (map block), `HUMANS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SZMELC.md`, `META.md`.

<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/DESIGN-MD.md -->
## Design docs & agent briefs
> Load when: starting a project, writing a brief for a coding agent, or changing a project's architecture.

| File | Written by | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `DESIGN.md` | Owner, own words | Raw intent: what, for whom, why; constraints; nice-to-haves marked as such. Agents never rewrite it. |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE-v<N>.md` | Agent + owner | Binding contract for major version N: paths, config, CLI, storage, tests. |
| `docs/<NAME>-SPEC.md` | Agent + owner | Contract between a runtime and its extensions (addons, plugins, drivers). |
| `<SOURCE>.md` | Human | External source document an implementation follows. |

- Read `DESIGN.md` and the current architecture contract before changing anything.
- A change that deviates from the contract updates the contract in the same commit.
- Briefs: ordered phases, each with a literal acceptance criterion; a phase starts only when the previous one passes; report after each.
- Build a thin working vertical slice first, never broad stubs.
- List fixed tech decisions with a one-line reason each, and one anchor example (config, CLI session) the implementation must match.
- Ambiguity → the simplest option that satisfies the brief, assumption stated inline, keep going.
- "Reproducible" means repeatable from the same inputs unless bit-for-bit is stated.

<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/INDEX-MD.md -->
## Lazy-load indexes
> Load when: generating, reading or changing INDEX.md, index.json or an all-in-one rule bundle.

- Generated by the build script from file headers (line 1 title, line 2 `> Load when:`), with a "generated, do not edit" comment under the title. Never hand-edit; the build's `--check` mode fails CI when stale.
- `INDEX.md`: `# Index`, a read-once instruction, then `| File | Load when |` tables per section: Always on, Cores, Rules, Skills, Experimental (opt-in only), Legacy (title only).
- `index.json`: `name`, `repo`, `entries[]` with `path`, `title`, `load_when`, `status` (`always|stable|experimental|legacy`), `kind` (`global|core|skill|rule|archive`); schema `META/schema/index.schema.json`.
- Bundle (`CONVENTIONS.md`): map of the rule tree, then every stable rule inlined, headings demoted one level, each after a `<!-- source: <path> -->` marker. For tools that cannot lazy-load; never loaded together with the index.
- Agents read `INDEX.md` once per session, then only files whose trigger matches; never bulk-read, never `@import` rule files into always-on instructions.
- Web index of the same entries: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LLMS-TXT.md`. Maps per core: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/CORE-MAPS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/RULE-FILES.md -->
## Rule files
> Load when: writing, naming or reviewing a convention rule file.

- Line 1 `# Title`, line 2 `> Load when: <concrete trigger>`; generators read both (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/INDEX-MD.md`). Skeleton `META/templates/rule.md`.
- One topic per file, one rule per line: imperative one-liners (`- ...`); a table only when denser than lines.
- ~5–20 lines; longer → split the topic.
- No prose, no filler adjectives; rationale only when the rule is non-obvious.
- Paths: categories and topic files UPPERCASE kebab (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- A rule about a named file `X.ext` is `X-EXT.md` (`AGENTS-MD.md`, `LLMS-TXT.md`), so harnesses and GitHub never mistake it for the file itself.
- Never duplicate a rule: reference the owning file by backticked repo path; every backticked path must exist.
- Status by directory, not by field: `EXPERIMENTAL/` opt-in, `LEGACY/` archive (line 3 `> Superseded by: <path>`), else stable; stable rules never reference either.
- State rules generically; project specifics go in that project's README or `AGENTS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/AGENTS-MD.md -->
## Agent instruction files
> Load when: creating or editing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, or Cursor/Copilot/Kiro/Windsurf rules in any project.

- Standard: <https://agents.md/>. Canonical `AGENTS.md` at the project root; add one per subdir only when a subtree has its own rules.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `QWEN.md`: a single line `@AGENTS.md` (import). Never duplicate content.
- Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, Zed, Jules and Amp read `AGENTS.md` natively; add tool-specific files only when a tool needs frontmatter.
- Tool-specific files (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, `.kiro/steering/*.md`): generate from a source, never hand-edit copies. `./install.sh project <dir>` drops the Szmelc ones.
- Never keep two diverging copies (e.g. `CLAUDE.md` with the tool name swapped); one source, imports elsewhere.
- Content: only what an agent cannot infer — build/test/lint commands, layout map, project-specific rules, gotchas.
- Never restate global conventions; reference them by path in this repo (`CONVENTIONS/INTERFACES/CLI.md`).
- Project baseline: read `DESIGN.md` and the current architecture contract first; finish every change; tests on throwaway state; a deviation updates the contract in the same commit (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/ORIGINAL/DESIGN-MD.md`).
- Imperative one-liners. Over ~150 lines → split per subdir.
- Skeleton: `META/templates/AGENTS.md`. Related: `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SKILL-MD.md`, `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/MCP-JSON.md`, `CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LLMS-TXT.md`.

<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CHANGELOG-MD.md -->
## Changelog
> Load when: creating or updating CHANGELOG.md, or preparing a release in a project that keeps one.

- Format: Keep a Changelog 1.1 <https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/>. File `CHANGELOG.md` at the root, when the project keeps one (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- Top: `# Changelog`, then `## [Unreleased]`, then releases newest first as `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Entries under `### Added`, `### Changed`, `### Deprecated`, `### Removed`, `### Fixed`, `### Security`; omit empty groups.
- One line per user-visible change, written for users; no commit hashes, no internal refactors.
- Add the entry under `[Unreleased]` in the same PR as the change.
- Release: rename `[Unreleased]` to the version and date, open a new empty `[Unreleased]`.
- Compare links at the bottom: `[Unreleased]: <repo>/compare/vX.Y.Z...HEAD`, `[x.y.z]: <repo>/compare/vPREV...vX.Y.Z`.
- The release section becomes the tag message and release notes (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CODE-OF-CONDUCT-MD.md -->
## Code of conduct
> Load when: adding a code of conduct to a repo or organization, or opening a project to outside contributors.

- Adopt the Contributor Covenant <https://www.contributor-covenant.org/> by reference: `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` with its unmodified text, or a link to the adopted version plus the enforcement contact.
- Org-wide default: one `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` in the org `.github` repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`); repos override only when they differ.
- A repo copy only for community repos (outside contributors, Discussions); solo tools rely on the org default.
- Enforcement contact: a project or org channel, never a personal address.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CODEOWNERS.md -->
## Code owners
> Load when: adding or editing CODEOWNERS, or requiring owner review on pull requests.

- File `.github/CODEOWNERS` <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners>; GitHub also reads root and `docs/`, keep one.
- Only with ≥ 2 maintainers or when a ruleset requires code-owner review; solo repos skip it.
- Line: gitignore-style pattern, then owners; the last matching line wins.
- `*` default line first, narrower paths below it.
- Owners: teams (`@org/team`) over people; every owner needs write access.
- Required owner review: ruleset `pull_request` with `require_code_owner_review: true` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/SETTINGS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/CONTRIBUTING-MD.md -->
## Contributing guide
> Load when: creating or editing a project's CONTRIBUTING.md.

- GitHub community health file <https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/setting-guidelines-for-repository-contributors>: `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the root, `.github/` or `docs/`; GitHub links it when someone opens an issue or PR.
- Org-wide default in the org `.github` repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`); a repo copy only when the project differs.
- Content, short: setup, build/test/check commands, the branch → PR flow by pointer (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md`, `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PULL-REQUESTS.md`), where to ask.
- Same commands as `AGENTS.md`; change both in the same commit.
- Vulnerabilities never go through issues: point to `SECURITY.md` (`CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SECURITY-MD.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LICENSE.md -->
## License file
> Load when: adding or changing a project's license file, or writing license fields in manifests.

- Which license: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/REPO/METADATA.md`.
- File `LICENSE` at the root, no extension; full unmodified text (<https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit/>) so GitHub detects it.
- Copyright line: `Copyright (c) <year> <holder>`; year of first publication, holder = the publishing org or author.
- Manifests use the SPDX id: `PKGBUILD` `license=('MIT')`, `flake.nix` `meta.license = lib.licenses.mit`, `package.json` `"license": "MIT"`, `SKILL.md` `license: MIT`.
- Packages install the file (`CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`).
- Forks keep the upstream license and copyright line; add yours below it.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/LLMS-TXT.md -->
## llms.txt
> Load when: publishing docs or a site meant for LLMs, or generating an llms.txt.

- Standard: <https://llmstxt.org/>. File `llms.txt` at the site root, next to `index.html` (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/DEPLOYMENTS/GITHUB-PAGES.md`).
- Order: `# Name` (the only required part), `> one-line summary`, optional plain paragraphs, then `## Section` link lists.
- Link line: `- [Title](url): what it holds or when to read it`.
- `## Optional`: links an agent may skip when context is short.
- Link Markdown sources (raw files, `.md` pages), not rendered HTML.
- Generated by the build script from the same sources as the site and index; never hand-written or hand-edited; CI fails on a stale copy.
- `llms-full.txt` (every linked document inlined): optional extension outside the spec; generate it the same way when shipped.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/MCP-JSON.md -->
## MCP server config
> Load when: adding, sharing or committing MCP server configuration (.mcp.json) in a project.

- File `.mcp.json` at the project root with a `mcpServers` map; project scope as defined by Claude Code <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp>. Commit it so every contributor gets the same servers.
- Stdio entry: `command`, `args`, `env`. Remote entry: `"type": "http"`, `url`, optional `headers`; an entry without `type` is read as stdio.
- Commit only servers that need no secrets or read them from the environment: `${VAR}`, `${VAR:-default}` (expanded in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers`).
- Never write a literal key or token into it; servers with personal credentials go to local or user scope, never the repo.
- One server per capability, short lowercase name; pin package versions in `args`, never `@latest`.
- Interactive sessions ask before using project servers; `claude -p`, SDK and cloud sessions load them without asking, so review `.mcp.json` changes like code.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/README-MD.md -->
## README
> Load when: writing or editing a project README.

- English. Truthful: every feature and dependency listed exists; update it in the same change as the code.
- Top: `# Name`, one bold sentence saying what it is, the one-line install, badges (`CONVENTIONS/DESIGN/COLORS.md`).
- Then, skipping empty ones: Usage, How it works, Configuration, Packaging, License.
- Install: package first (SAUR `pacman -S`, `nix run`); never distro-by-distro package-manager blocks; elevation via `pkexec`.
- No `curl … | bash` from a branch tip; point at a tag or a signed script.
- State limits, risks and trust boundaries plainly: what leaves the machine, who can reach a key.
- Plain headings for structure; no blockquote-as-heading, no `\` line breaks, no version in the title.
- Polish readers → separate `README-PL.md`; one language per file (`CONVENTIONS/REPO/WRITING.md`).
- Remove agent leftovers ("CONSOLIDATED DELIVERABLE", "Here is…", "As an AI…") before committing.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SECURITY-MD.md -->
## Security policy
> Load when: creating or editing SECURITY.md, or setting up vulnerability reporting.

- GitHub community health file <https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/getting-started/adding-a-security-policy-to-your-repository>: `SECURITY.md` in the root, `.github/` or `docs/`; org default in the org `.github` repo (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/ORGANIZATIONS.md`).
- `## Supported versions`: table of version ranges and whether they get fixes; usually the latest release only.
- `## Reporting a vulnerability`: GitHub private vulnerability reporting (Security tab → Report a vulnerability); enable it per `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/CODE-SECURITY.md`.
- Never ask for vulnerability reports in public issues, discussions or chat.
- Response expectations with numbers: acknowledgement time, status updates, target fix time; reporter credited in the advisory unless they decline.
- Fix in the advisory's temporary private fork; publish the advisory with the patch release (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/TAGS.md`).
- No personal email addresses; any other private channel belongs to the project or org.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/SPECS/THIRD-PARTY/SKILL-MD.md -->
## Skills (SKILL.md)
> Load when: writing, editing, or installing an agent skill.

- Layout: `<name>/SKILL.md` + optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`. Directory name == `name`.
- Frontmatter: `name` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, ≤ 64), `description` (≤ 1024: what it does + when to use, with trigger words). Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string map), `allowed-tools`.
- Body < ~500 lines. Push detail into `references/` and link it relatively (progressive disclosure).
- One capability per skill. Deterministic steps go in `scripts/`, not prose.
- Install by symlinking the directory into each harness skill root (`./install.sh` knows them). Never copy.
- Skeleton: `META/templates/SKILL.md`. Validate with `META/tools/check.sh` rules: name/dir match, description length.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md -->
## Branches
> Load when: creating branches, opening/merging PRs, releasing, or promoting/deprecating a convention.

- `main` is the only long-lived branch: current stable truth; installs track it. No direct commits.
- Every change: short-lived branch off `main` → PR into `main` → merge → delete the branch.
- Name by intent: `feat/<x>`, `fix/<x>`, `docs/<x>`, `chore/<x>`, `experimental/<x>`, `legacy/<x>`; private staging: `local/<x>`.

| Prefix | Use for | Scope (CI-enforced) |
|---|---|---|
| `feat/*` `fix/*` `docs/*` `chore/*` | Stable changes | Any source file |
| `experimental/*` | New or changed proposals | `CONVENTIONS/EXPERIMENTAL/` + generated files |
| `legacy/*` | Archiving superseded material | `CONVENTIONS/LEGACY/` + generated files |
| `local/*` | Private or unverified material awaiting review | Never pushed, never merged |

- Merge: `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`; keep one topic per PR so the squash reads as one change.
- Stale branch with no open PR and nothing ahead of `main`: delete it.
- Promote: move `CONVENTIONS/EXPERIMENTAL/<x>.md` to `CONVENTIONS/<category>/<x>.md` in a `feat/*` PR.
- Demote: move to `CONVENTIONS/LEGACY/` in a `legacy/*` PR; add `> Superseded by: <path>` as line 3. Legacy files are never deleted.
- `local/*`: one commit per proposal; never pushed (pre-push hook `META/tools/hooks/pre-push`, enable with `git config core.hooksPath META/tools/hooks`); CI rejects it. Approved commits are re-applied on a `feat/*` or `experimental/*` branch after review; rejected ones stay local.
- CI enforces prefix scope (`META/tools/lane-check.sh`).
- Projects that ship releases: `main` = stable, other branches = `-ex` builds; channels and tags: `CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/CHANNELS.md`.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/COMMITS.md -->
## Commits
> Load when: writing a commit message, PR title, or squash-merge title.

- English, imperative, one subject line ≤ 72 chars; body only when the why is not obvious.
- Type prefix with optional scope: `feat(saur): …`, `fix(core): …`, `docs: …`, `ci: …`, `chore: …`, `refactor: …`, `test: …`.
- Version bump → append the version: `feat: signed package lists (0.3.1)`.
- Never web-UI defaults (`Update README.md`, `Create file`) on `main`.
- One topic per commit and per PR; the squash title follows the same format (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/BRANCHES.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/FINISH.md -->
## Finish every change
> Load when: finishing a feature or fix, before calling work done.

- Done means everything the change touches is done; never leave half a feature for later.
- Carry it through the code, the `--help` text (global and per command) and the shell completions.
- Carry it through the docs (`README.md`, config comments, architecture contract) and packaging (`CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/ARCH.md`, `CONVENTIONS/PACKAGING/NIX.md`).
- Version bump → every copy at once (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/RELEASES/VERSIONING.md`).
- Then verify on real data (`CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/VERIFICATION.md`) and get green CI before reporting (`CONVENTIONS/GITHUB/PULL-REQUESTS.md`).

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/NOTIFY.md -->
## Notifications
> Load when: a job runs > ~10 min, or a failure needs a human.

- Tool: `dc-notify` (`-h` for help). Embed with outcome title; `-s ok|fail|warn|run`; fields `-F "k|v"`; links `-b "label|url"`.
- Send on long-job start + end, and on failures needing a human.
- `-p` pings the owner: critical only.
- Webhooks and user IDs live in the tool's local config (`$DC_WEBHOOK` or the user config dir); never in a repo.

---
<!-- source: CONVENTIONS/WORKFLOW/VERIFICATION.md -->
## Verification
> Load when: any code change.

- Prove it works with the cheapest real check: build, run, hit the path.
- Run existing tests covering touched code; full suite only for cross-cutting changes.
- New tests only for: non-trivial logic, regressions, parsers, security boundaries, public APIs.
- Never: tests for glue/getters/one-off scripts, tests of tests, mocks of mocks, tests that re-assert the implementation.
- Tests and experiments use throwaway state (temp `HOME`, config dir, DB, `GNUPGHOME`); never the real config, data or keys.
- Shell: `bash -n`/`sh -n` and `shellcheck` before delivery (`CONVENTIONS/CODE/SHELL.md`).
- Never claim "works" unchecked. Unverifiable → say so.
